notes.rule: reviewer — correctness patterns
notes.claim: the Holiday rows and the HolidayImport record that together make a country `sourced` are written in two unrelated statements with no transaction, so a failure between them leaves rows written and the country still reported unsourced

witness.detail: sync() calls writeEntries (line 207), which issues one prisma.holiday.create per accepted entry, and only then calls recordImport (line 218). A connection drop or a non-P2002 database error after the fifth of ten inserts propagates out of sync() as a 500 with five Holiday rows committed and no HolidayImport row. The country then reads `unsourced` from sourcingBlock, REQ-02-012 makes the screen issue a fresh sync on the next load, and that sync re-fetches. The state does converge — REQ-02-006 skips the five already-written dates and REQ-02-021 records the offered count — so no row is duplicated and nothing is double-paid. Recorded as a note because the recovery is named by the spec and the spec states no transaction requirement for the import, explicitly taking no lock (Edge case 12).

notes.suggestedFix: none required against the document; if it is wanted, wrap one country's writes and its import record in a single prisma.$transaction — the provider call is already outside it, so nothing awaits the network inside

notes.rule: reviewer — resource handling on the failure path
notes.claim: on a non-2xx answer the response body is neither read nor cancelled, so the socket is held until garbage collection

witness.detail: The provider answers 503 for 2026/IN. Line 41 throws without touching response.body, and the finally at line 60 clears the abort timer, so nothing ever aborts the request either. notes.rule: REQ-02-012 — the screen syncs without being asked
notes.claim: a year whose auto-sync was abandoned by a tab switch is marked synced and is never synced again for the life of the page

witness.detail: autoSynced.current.add(year) (line 405) runs BEFORE runSyncRef.current(...), and the effect's cleanup aborts that request when year changes. An admin opens 2026 with both countries unsourced, the sync is issued, and within the provider's call bound they click the 2027 tab: the cleanup aborts controller A and runSync catches AbortError and returns. Clicking back to 2026 re-reads the list; if the aborted request did not reach the server or its writes did not land, sourcing still reports the countries unsourced and needsSync is true again — but autoSynced.current.has(2026) short-circuits the effect at line 404. The year then sits behind the uncovered banner with no sync issued until Refresh is pressed or the page is reloaded, which is the click REQ-02-012 says must not be needed. In practice the server usually completes the handler after a client abort, which masks it — hence a note rather than a claim of certain breakage.

notes.suggestedFix: record the year in autoSynced when the sync answers rather than when it is issued, and delete the entry on abort

notes.rule: sweep 4 — an untrusted value that should have been discarded is stored instead
notes.claim: the date filter accepts a day of 1-31 in any month, so an impossible date is accepted rather than discarded and is written on a different day from the one the provider sent

witness.detail: The month/day guard is `if (month < 1 || month > 12 || day < 1 || day > 31)`, so '2026-02-30' and '2026-04-31' pass Rule 4 and are pushed into accepted. The consumer is asUtcDate in apps/api/src/holidays/holiday-sourcing.service.ts:470 — new Date(`${date}T00:00:00.000Z`) — and its value goes straight to prisma.holiday.create at line 357. I ran `node -e "console.log(new Date('2026-02-30T00:00:00.000Z').toString())"` and it printed 'Mon Mar 02 2026 03:00:00 GMT+0300', so the date does not become an Invalid Date that throws: it silently rolls over and a paid holiday is stored on 2 March. That is a stored row claiming a day the provider never offered, where Validation Rules 4-6 promise 'A provider entry that fails any of them is discarded and counted in `discarded`'. Neither shipped driver produces such a date and the double's malformedShape exercises a long name and a wrong year but not an impossible day, which is why this is a note. (Shard 3 raised this with a witness saying the value becomes an Invalid Date; that mechanism is wrong and the corrected one is above.)

notes.suggestedFix: reject a day the month does not have — a round-trip check that the parsed date re-serializes to the same string — and add an impossible-date entry to the double's malformed shape

notes.rule: an abandoned read leaves the summary claiming it is still loading
notes.claim: `loadSummary` sets `summaryLoading` true and returns on an abort without ever clearing it, and the auto-sync effect aborts that signal at the moment its own success flips `needsSync` false — so a successful automatic sync can leave the summary block on its preloader until the year tab moves. `runSync` guards exactly this with a run counter in `finally`; the two reads it drives do not.

witness.detail: An admin opens Settings › Holidays on a year whose countries are all unsourced. The effect at page.tsx:404-411 issues runSync with `controller.signal` and returns `() => controller.abort()`. runSync awaits `Promise.all([load(signal), loadSummary(signal)])` (:371). `load` resolves first and calls setSourcing with a block in which every country is now `sourced` (:211), so `needsSync` (:397-400) flips to false; React commits that render and runs the previous effect's cleanup, which aborts the signal `loadSummary` is still waiting on. In loadSummary, `setSummaryLoading(true)` ran at :283, the fetch rejects with AbortError, the catch at :302 returns before `setSummaryLoading(false)` at :306, and the trailing `if (signal?.aborted) return` guards it too. Nothing re-runs loadSummary for the same year — the read effect's deps are `load`/`loadSummary`, whose identities depend only on orgId/year/country — so HolidaySummary keeps rendering the Preloader branch (HolidaySummary.tsx:46) with the figures sitting on the server. I verified each line and the effect ordering rather than taking the shard's word. Kept as a note, not raised to a blocker, for two reasons: the window is the few milliseconds between `load`'s commit and the summary response, and the paths that reach it — TC-02-E2E-01 and TC-02-E2E-04, both of which sync a set that ends fully `sourced` — are recorded green in stages/implement.attempt-4.md ('20 passed'), so the race does not reproduce in the reference environment; and CR-18's 'class of call sites' is a reading of one unhandled path rather than a mechanism plainly missing at several. A slower summary read than list read is what makes it fire, which is a loaded database.

notes.suggestedFix: clear `summaryLoading` (and `loading`) in a `finally` guarded by a run counter, the way runSync guards `setSyncing` at page.tsx:381 — its own comment states the rule: 'a run that was abandoned must not leave one up forever'

notes.rule: the year guard is applied to the summary and not to the warning beside it

witness.detail: A member resolves to IN, which the provider refuses. Under the current year the banner carries `holiday-sourcing-uncovered-IN` with `countryNotCovered`. The admin clicks the tab for year+1, for which IN was recorded `empty` by an earlier sync: `load(signal)` for the new year is in flight and `sourcing` still holds the old year's block, so page.tsx:584-585 keeps drawing the IN line with `countryNotCovered` under a year whose state is `empty` — the very sentence Edge case 5a says that state must never carry. The summary beside it now correctly waits (HolidaySummary.tsx:46), which is what makes the two disagree on screen at the same instant. `isEmpty` at :583 reads the same stale `hasUnsourced`.

notes.rule: contracts §Validation Rules row 4 vs the filter that now ships
notes.claim: The code now discards a provider date that names a day its month does not have; the document's Rule 4 still states the constraint as the format and the year only, so the two disagree about what a conforming entry is and the document is the weaker statement.

witness.detail: contracts.md:195 — '| 4 | A provider entry's `date` | `YYYY-MM-DD` and inside the requested year | discarded silently, counted | yes |'. Against it, packages/validation/src/holiday-sourcing.ts:190-196 adds isRealCalendarDay, which round-trips the value through a UTC Date and requires the same string back, and :239 discards when it fails; holiday-sourcing.test.ts:210-219 pins that `2026-02-31` is discarded. Under the document as written that entry passes Rule 4 and the §Decision table's first row then creates a Holiday for it. The code's reading is the better one — asUtcDate (holiday-sourcing.service.ts:470) rolls `2026-02-31` to 3 March, so the document's reading stores a paid day the provider never offered — which is why this is addressed to the document rather than to the code, and why it is a note: an implementation satisfying the document literally exists, it is just the wrong one.

notes.suggestedFix: state Rule 4 as '`YYYY-MM-DD`, a day that exists, and inside the requested year'

notes.rule: the prose under a table counts its rows

notes.rule: the document is silent where the code now decides
notes.claim: Keying `byCurrency` on financial settings rather than on the accumulated map is the better reading and closes pass 1's S1-N2, but it produces a body shape the bundle names nowhere — a member who holds settings and whom no holiday reached now carries `byCurrency: []` — and that rule now lives only in the code and in an integration test with no case id.

witness.detail: REQ-02-018 ('IF a member has no financial settings, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL omit their amounts entirely') and contracts.md:125 ('It is **absent** — not empty, not null — on a member with no financial settings') both speak only of the member without settings, so neither forbids the empty list; holiday-summary.service.ts:270 now sends it, pinned by apps/api/test/holiday-sourcing.spec.ts:762-766 under no numbered case. notes.rule: a bound proportional to the call bound also has to cover the writes in the same request
notes.claim: The tightened margin is right in intent — a fixed +5000ms passed against a service that ignored the configured bound — but `callBoundMs * 4` is 1200ms measured around the whole HTTP request, which also signs in, resolves the country set, writes 14 Polish holidays one create at a time and records two imports. Roughly three quarters of the budget belongs to work the bound says nothing about, so a loaded database and a timing regression now fail the same way.

witness.detail: apps/api/test/holiday-sourcing.spec.ts:806 sets provider.callBoundMs = 300; :814 asserts elapsed < callBoundMs * 4 over `sync(...)`, which performs the PL import (14 rows through writeEntries' per-date existence check) and the IN abandonment in one request. The previous assertion was callBoundMs + 5000.

notes.suggestedFix: time the mechanism rather than the request — a sync whose only country is `neverAnswers` has no writes to pay for, and `callBoundMs * 4` over that is a bound on the deadline itself

notes.rule: the comment names a different mechanism from the one the line performs
notes.claim: The comment says 'Read the body to completion before abandoning it'; the line cancels the body, which is the correct way to release the socket and is not what the sentence describes. The behaviour is right — this closes pass 1's S2-N3 — and only the comment is wrong, on the line a reader consults before changing it.

witness.detail: apps/api/src/holidays/provider/nager-holiday.provider.ts:42-45 — the comment above `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined);`. Optional chaining short-circuits the whole call chain when `response.body` is null, so the null case is safe, the `.catch` swallows a cancel racing the abort, and the throw still reaches REQ-02-009's unsourced path. The non-array branch below needs no equivalent because `response.json()` has already drained the body.

notes.suggestedFix: 'Release the body before abandoning the response' — a cancel is a release, not a read
